extracted.intended_audience: Open-source investigators in Bellingcat / GLAN Justice & Accountability Unit working on Ukraine investigations (investigators, reviewers, legal advisors, team leads)
extracted.subtask_description: Methodology and operational standards for conducting online open source investigations (OOSI) into incidents in Ukraine, including steps to mitigate technical, access and cognitive bias, data protection and special handling of sexual and gender-based violence material.

rubrics_metrics.name: Impartial and comprehensive evidence collection
rubrics_metrics.description: Any investigation leading to the collection of evidence needs to be as impartial and comprehensive as possible so as to be fair to the person against whom the evidence is ultimately used.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This methodology takes measures to mitigate against bias and expects investigations to be conducted to standards approximating official investigators where possible; fairness to subjects is central to admissibility and ethical practice.

rubrics_metrics.name: Mitigate algorithmic effects through varied searches
rubrics_metrics.description: The effects of search engine and social media algorithms are a consideration in OOSI. Open source investigators should counterbalance algorithmic biases by applying methodologies to ensure search results are as diverse as possible.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use advanced and varied search terms, run multiple search queries, use a variety of search engines, incorporate neutral and partisan search terms, and search in multiple languages to surface niche/local/examinable content and avoid relying on default algorithmic delivery. (Cites Berkeley Protocol: browser/search engine/syntax can lead to very different results.)

rubrics_metrics.name: Use targeted and sophisticated search queries
rubrics_metrics.description: The active nature of OOSI searches and levels of specificity interfere with default algorithmic functions; targeted, sophisticated queries narrow index scope and better surface relevant content.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Combine neutral and partisan terms and use multiple languages; specific queries reduce number of indexed pages the algorithm must rank and help find local, low-traffic, partisan or first-hand content that mainstream users would not see.

rubrics_metrics.name: Leverage algorithmic profiling deliberately
rubrics_metrics.description: Algorithmic tracking of user preferences can be an advantage for OOSI because search algorithms will learn researcher preferences over time and surface more relevant local/niche material.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Be aware that newly created research accounts may initially receive mainstream results (example: ~one week for an account to learn local content); the project accepts some algorithmic tracking as operationally useful rather than attempting to eliminate it entirely.

rubrics_metrics.name: Search engine and browser choices
rubrics_metrics.description: Different browsers, search engines and search syntax can produce different results. Berkeley Protocol recommends alternative browsers; Bellingcat uses Hunchly in Google Chrome and has decided not to use multiple browsers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Balance theoretical reduction of technical bias through multiple browsers against practical collection requirements (e.g., Hunchly collection constraints). Use Google and Yandex and any other search engines investigators see fit.

rubrics_metrics.name: VPN use policy
rubrics_metrics.description: VPNs are used to disguise the IP address and protect the traffic of the user; they affect algorithmic delivery because exit-node IPs can influence results.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use VPNs primarily for security and to avoid using investigators' real IP addresses. Recognise VPNs swap one known factor for an unknown one (other users of exit node influence results). Default policy: set exit node to United States to maximise access to content (e.g., some Russian state media available in U.S. accounts). Do not assume VPN hides browsing history or signed-in state.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cookies and browsing data policy
rubrics_metrics.description: Cookies track users across sites and can affect displayed information; deleting cookies could mitigate algorithmic selection but has operational costs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not systematically remove cookies and browsing data before investigative sessions because deletion is a red flag to platforms and can lead to rapid deletion of research accounts. Deleting cookies does not remove data collected while signed in. Balance algorithmic considerations against account stability.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of passive research accounts
rubrics_metrics.description: Research accounts are needed to log into social media platforms. Bellingcat investigators do not use their true identities.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reasons: protect researcher identity (avoid accidental likes/alerts), protect subjects/sources (prevent evidence deletion or risk to sources), and mitigate some algorithmic selection. Do not use personal accounts; use stable passive research accounts rather than creating fresh accounts for every investigation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Limitations on generating fresh accounts
rubrics_metrics.description: Continually generating new social media accounts is time-consuming and can trigger platform bot/inauthentic behaviour detection.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Maintain stable, credible passive accounts to avoid deletion. Recognise fingerprinting (browser version, language, time settings, window size, cookies, VPN) can still identify a user attempting many inauthentic accounts; excessive account creation may result in permanent prevention.

rubrics_metrics.name: Security tooling: Privacy Badger and similar
rubrics_metrics.description: Privacy Badger is a plugin designed to prevent third party trackers from tracking websites visited by a user.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Install Privacy Badger primarily for security reasons to make it more difficult for websites to identify the user and reduce tracking that could compromise research accounts or investigator safety.

rubrics_metrics.name: Access bias awareness and mitigation
rubrics_metrics.description: Not all actors have equal access to mainstream social media platforms (e.g., elderly, those in internet shutdowns, coerced users, or silenced critics). Platforms may also limit certain content (e.g., Russian state media).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Mitigate by using neutral and varied search terms, searching both Russian and Ukrainian social media and groups, and actively seeking pro-Russian as well as pro-Ukrainian sources where possible.

rubrics_metrics.name: Human/cognitive bias mitigation procedures
rubrics_metrics.description: Cognitive biases can lead investigators to over-focus on certain information and under-focus on others; these cannot be eliminated but must be mitigated.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Adopt procedures: begin investigations with no settled hypothesis; actively pursue all lines of inquiry (e.g., search for military justifications); search all platforms including pro-Russian groups; perform intensive verification on each piece of content regardless of source orientation; work through the methodology's list of questions to avoid skipped lines of inquiry; separate inducted investigators from non-inducted staff; have separate review by team leader and legal team.

rubrics_metrics.name: Separation of roles, responsibilities and review
rubrics_metrics.description: Defined roles (lead investigator, first-instance investigators, reviewing investigators, legal leads, ad-hoc consultants) and separation between inducted investigators and other personnel.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure coordination with legal on procedure design; inducted investigators carry out J&A investigations while non-inducted investigators and leadership do not; investigations are subject to separate review by team leader and legal team to mitigate perception or risk of bias.

rubrics_metrics.name: No deception / passive-only policy for joining closed groups
rubrics_metrics.description: Policy of passive research only: no joining of closed groups through active deception (e.g., pretending to be pro-Russian or otherwise lying), and no engaging with individuals directly (no befriending or messaging).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Closed groups may be joined only when effective authorisation is achieved and after a case-by-case legal assessment. Do not use actual identity or 'Bellingcat' affiliation when attempting to join unless assessed and recorded; prefer benign/neutral labelled accounts or explicitly labelled 'Bellingcat Research Account' where appropriate and approved.

rubrics_metrics.name: Criteria for permissible joining of closed groups
rubrics_metrics.description: Some closed groups may be considered effectively open or joinable without deception under certain conditions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Permissible examples: invitation requirement is only a bot-screening device; group size/membership effectively imposes no criteria; group can be joined with a benign/neutral account; disclosure in request that investigator is a 'western' open source investigator may constitute effective authorisation; if a 'Bellingcat Research Account' is used and granted access, withdraw it and join with an alias to establish authorisation without deception. Assess legality in jurisdiction where evidence is intended to be used.

rubrics_metrics.name: Recordkeeping for closed groups joined
rubrics_metrics.description: Maintain a list of closed groups which have been joined and the rationale for joining them.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: List should include group name, platform, number of members, justification and link. This supports accountability and legal review.

rubrics_metrics.name: Procedure for closed groups requiring deception to access
rubrics_metrics.description: Where a particularly important closed group cannot be joined without deception, the project will develop procedures.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Plan includes coordination with official authorities to pass the account to them or otherwise facilitate their access using Bellingcat’s accounts or contextual knowledge so investigators do not gain unauthorised access by deception.

rubrics_metrics.name: Data protection, privacy and GDPR compliance
rubrics_metrics.description: The project must comply with the letter and spirit of the GDPR and adhere to general data protection principles.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Engage specialist data protection lawyers; maintain a controlled data management system including relevant risk assessments; develop written policies and agreements with external organisations in light of counsel advice; be mindful that certain methods (e.g., misrepresentation) have GDPR implications and potential criminal law consequences under local law (e.g., Computer Misuse Act in U.K.).

rubrics_metrics.name: Special handling and 'do no harm' approach to SGBV material
rubrics_metrics.description: SGBV is sensitive, frequently present in conflict content, and open source information alone is insufficient to fully investigate these crimes. The J&A Unit takes a 'do no harm' approach and conducts gender analysis for each major investigation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Integrate gender perspective across investigations (not as an afterthought); create separate investigation plans for SGBV incidents with tailored search terms (including colloquial terms); store SGBV and crimes against children content in highly secure manner; arrange UWAZI database so such content can be filtered and access-controlled.

rubrics_metrics.name: SGBV definitions and gender/inclusion frameworks
rubrics_metrics.description: Adopt clear definitions for gender, gender-based violence, sexual violence, gender-based crimes, sexual crimes, gender perspective, gender analysis, and an intersectional approach.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use established international definitions (e.g., Rome Statute, UN OHCHR, International Protocol, ICC OTP) and apply intersectional analysis to contextualise acts and understand gravity. Incorporate these definitions into investigative framing and reporting.

rubrics_metrics.name: Language use and linguistic resourcing
rubrics_metrics.description: Investigators will search in English, Ukrainian and Russian using terms standardised relative to the investigation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Russian- and Ukrainian-speaking investigators assist English-only investigators to ensure search terms are varied and appropriate for material encountered; ensure searches use both languages and multiple search engines (Google, Yandex).

rubrics_metrics.name: Active search methodology (no passive scrolling)
rubrics_metrics.description: Simple surface-level searches or passive scrolling are unacceptable for investigation or verification activities.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Investigators must deploy an investigation methodology calculated to surface relevant content (targeted queries, multi-engine searches, multilingual terms) rather than relying on algorithmic feeds encountered by casual users.

rubrics_metrics.name: Intensive verification irrespective of source orientation
rubrics_metrics.description: Perform intensive verification on each piece of content whether it is posted by pro-Ukraine or pro-Russian sources.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Verification must be systematic and equal across partisan origins; do not allow source orientation to determine rigor of verification.
